transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-02
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Nina Cho (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood CSM), Jared Mills (Ironwood Dir MLOps), Priya Raman (Ironwood Cloud Eng), Elena Torres (Ironwood Head of Platform), Marco Velez (Ironwood Security)

Summary:
Quick intake to align on onboarding runway for Ironwood's platform activation — focus areas: network/VPC peering, KMS/encryption, pilot benchmark for latency/cost, runbook/timing for production cutover, success criteria and owners. Agreed to a 2-week pilot window mid-August.

Topics:
- Intro & roles
- Current infra and constraints (on-prem vs cloud, hybrid)
- Security/compliance expectations (KMS, audit logs, data residency)
- Pilot scope: throughput/latency targets, model selection, token cost expectations
- Integration pattern: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, service accounts, secrets
- Rollout plan and runbook share

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. we're, uh, Samir from Redwood, AE — joined by Nina our SE and Liam on success. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:10] Jared: Good, thanks. busy week but excited to get this kicked off.
[00:00:15] Priya: Hey — Priya here. We gave the pre-reads a scan. couple of questions but we'll go through.
[00:00:22] Elena: Hi all. want to make sure ops and security are part of the loop.
[00:00:28] Samir: Perfect. The goal for today is to align on runbook/ops intake, network requirements, and pilot benchmarks. we'll capture owners and next steps. Nina, want to do a quick technical intro?
[00:00:40] Nina: Sure. quick overview — Redwood Inference platform supports hosted, dedicated and private deploys; for Ironwood we discussed private/VPC option so I'll focus on that. We provide a private control plane, can do VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink, and we support KMS integration for envelope encryption. there's also our Dedicated pools if you want reserved capacity later on.
[00:01:05] Marco: Quick nit — when you said KMS envelope, do you mean customer-managed CMKs only or can Redwood manage keys? Our security policy prefers BYOK.
[00:01:14] Nina: Yes, by default we can support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via KMS. we also support HSM-backed keys in some private deployments. we'll send the KMS integration doc. note: sometimes the transcript had 'KMS' misheard as 'KMS-9' in pre-reads, sorry.
[00:01:30] Marco: hah, okay. good.
[00:01:33] Jared: On infra — we're hybrid. control plane in your cloud, workloads in our VPC in us-east-1. we want to avoid traffic egress charges and keep tokens in our environment. so the private plan is key.
[00:01:47] Samir: Understood. The private option will keep model execution inside your VPC; we'll set up a peering or private link. For throughput, what's your target QPS?
[00:01:59] Jared: initial pilot needs to handle 30 concurrent sessions, p99 latency under 350ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens). cost target is, uh, predictably below $0.0007 per token — but open to quantization + batching tradeoffs.
[00:02:17] Nina: Ok good. For the pilot we'll recommend a model variant and quantization profile — that should hit the latency/cost tradeoff. we'll run a bench to validate.
[00:02:25] [crosstalk] Priya: what model family were you thinking?
[00:02:28] Nina: For that latency range, we usually try a 13B quantized variant or a trimmed 30B in int4 depending on context length. we'll propose two runs.
[00:02:37] Elena: Side question — how do rollouts work? we want canary then full switch.
[00:02:41] Samir: We support canary rollouts per route in the Console. you can pin routes to model versions, do weighted traffic splits, and automatic fallback policies if capacity or errors spike. you'll get telemetry per route.
[00:02:55] Marco: Are audit logs exported to our SIEM? we need immutable logs for at least 90 days.
[00:03:01] Liam: Yes, we can stream audit logs to your S3/Kinesis or push to your SIEM via secure delivery. retention is configurable; we'll share the audit log playbook.
[00:03:10] Jared: Great. Another concern — data residency. Some prompt/data will be EU-resident only. can you pin regions per route?
[00:03:18] Nina: Yep. Smart routing supports region pinning and fallback. for private deployments we'll ensure the execution stays in the selected region.
[00:03:26] Priya: On the network pattern: peering vs PrivateLink — pros/cons? we prefer peering but our infra team likes PrivateLink for cross-account.
[00:03:34] Nina: Peering is simpler and lower latency, but traffic goes over the VPC peering link. PrivateLink gives more control and is easier with cross-account restrictions. depends on your security posture. We'll document both patterns and recommend PrivateLink if you have strict cross-account egress controls.
[00:03:50] [00:03:51] Marco: If we do PrivateLink, can we still do BYOK?
[00:03:55] Samir: Yes. BYOK is independent; key access is via KMS policies. we'll align IAM roles and policies in the runbook.
[00:04:02] Jared: Cool. let's talk timeline — we'd like pilot in mid-August, production by end of September. can we hit that?
[00:04:10] Samir: That timeline looks reasonable. this week we'll do onboarding docs; next week set up network; pilot window mid-August (we'll plan for two weeks to capture throughput and regression evals).
[00:04:21] Priya: For the network we need a contact at Redwood to coordinate peering.
[00:04:25] Samir: That will be Nina. Nina, you'll own peering checklist?
[00:04:28] Nina: Yep, I'll handle the peering checklist and share the CIDR guidance and security groups. we'll also include a preflight checklist (DNS, endpoints, route tables).
[00:04:39] [00:04:40] Priya: ok thanks.
[00:04:43] Marco: Security — do you have a SOC2 report and penetration test summary? we asked for them on the pre-read but didn't see an expiry date.
[00:04:50] Liam: We have a current SOC2 Type II report (expiry 2028-03) and latest pentest summary. I'll send those PDFs and the redacted report. also the SOC2 cover letter and the contact for audit questions.
[00:05:05] Marco: Good. also need to understand data at rest encryption and token handling. are model caches persisted on your side?
[00:05:12] Nina: Cache/kvcache is ephemeral per workload; in private deployment, the KV is kept inside your infra. We can disable caching if you prefer. Logs and blobs at rest are encrypted with your CMK.
[00:05:23] Jared: On cost — can you give us a sense of cost optimization levers? we will have bursts during peak hours.
[00:05:30] Samir: Sure — three levers: batching (increases throughput, may add minimal latency), quantization (reduces memory/cost at some quality tradeoff), and routing to cheaper model variants for non-sensitive routes. we also recommend prefix caching for repeated prompts. Redwood Optimize can give recommendations per workload.
[00:05:46] Priya: For pilot, we'll want a small set of prompts and a regression suite. who owns the evals?
[00:05:52] Nina: We'll propose a shared eval harness. Ironwood provides representative prompts, we run bench and quality checks, then iterate.
[00:05:59] Elena: can those evals include our SLAs and business metrics like token cost per session?
[00:06:05] Nina: absolutely, we'll surface token counts and cost breakdown in the Console; can tag runs per prompt set.
[00:06:11] [00:06:12] Jared: One more — latency numbers are for short prompts; for long context near 4k tokens what happens?
[00:06:18] Nina: for longer context, latency increases and throughput decreases; we'll recommend model variants or offloading via KV caching. also, our runtime picks kernels based on sequence distribution to optimize.
[00:06:30] Marco: We have a compliance question about PII — do you support filtering or redaction at the edge?
[00:06:36] Samir: We have integration examples with inline redaction pipelines. in many cases customers use a pre-processing layer in their VPC to strip PII before hitting Redwood. We can share patterns.
[00:06:47] Priya: Ok. the dev stack — do you provide terraform modules for infra setup?
[00:06:52] Nina: Yes, we have Terraform modules and CloudFormation templates. we'll share a starter repo link in the runbook. the modules configure peering, endpoints, IAM roles and KMS policies.
[00:07:03] Jared: About SLA — for Dedicated do you offer 99.9? we need high availability.
[00:07:08] Samir: Dedicated comes with SLA options. Hosted tiers have lower SLA. For enterprise Private deployments we can agree to 99.9 with planned maintenance windows. I'll include SLA options in the follow-up email.
[00:07:20] [00:07:21] Marco: Any customer references with similar compliance needs? healthcare/finance?
[00:07:25] Liam: Yes, we have a couple of healthcare and fintech customers using private deployments. I'll share redacted case studies and a short reference list.
[00:07:34] Elena: Great. On observability — we want per-token cost and latency breakdowns per route and per model. is that in Console?
[00:07:42] Nina: Yep — Console provides per-route dashboards, token-level cost, latency histograms and trace links. there is also an API for pulling daily cost reports.
[00:07:52] Jared: Would love to test the Console ahead of pilot. can we get a demo tenant?
[00:07:57] Samir: We can spin up a customer sandbox tenant for you; Liam will set that up and invite your team.
[00:08:03] Liam: I'll do that and include sample dashboards and the onboarding checklist.
[00:08:08] [00:08:09] Priya: about ingress — do you support mutual TLS for service endpoints?
[00:08:14] Nina: Yes, we support mTLS for service to service. we'll include cert rotation guidance.
[00:08:20] Jared: ok, let's recap owners quickly. Samir — pricing & SLA docs. Nina — peering checklist, terraform modules, benchmark plan. Liam — sandbox Console + SOC2 and pentest docs. Priya & Marco — provide network CIDRs, KMS owner and compliance docs. any additions?
[00:08:36] Marco: i'll also list the internal approval steps and timeline — need to know if pentest or SOC calls are required.
[00:08:42] Samir: noted.
[00:08:45] [00:08:46] Nina: One practical note — we recommend turning on prefix caching for your FAQ use-case; reduces token cost by up to 40% for repeated prompts.
[00:08:56] Priya: That's big. we'll include top-50 repeated prompts in the eval set.
[00:09:01] Jared: For the pilot, what are the acceptance criteria?
[00:09:05] Samir: Proposed acceptance: 1) p99 latency < 350ms on 90% of short prompt samples, 2) avg token cost below target for the chosen model variant, 3) successful integration with BYOK and network, 4) no critical security findings in quick audit checklist.
[00:09:22] Elena: Good. how will rollbacks work if we hit a regression in prod?
[00:09:26] Nina: We have automatic fallback policies and the ability to pin route to previous model version. plus canary keeper monitors. we'll also provide a rollback playbook.
[00:09:36] [00:09:37] Priya: Anything special about billing? monthly usage plus reserved capacity options?
[00:09:42] Samir: Yes. Hosted is pay-as-you-go. Dedicated/reserved has monthly commits and lower unit costs. we'll surface committed cost examples in the pricing doc; also burst options for Dedicated.
[00:09:54] Marco: ok — last sec question: what about on-prem air-gapped? we might explore later.
[00:09:59] Nina: We support on-prem packages for highly regulated workloads; that is a longer engagement (separate licensing). we can talk about that post-pilot if needed.
[00:10:08] Samir: ok folks, let's call out concrete next steps. I'll send the activation runbook and pricing, Nina will send terraform modules and the peering doc, Liam will share SOC2/pentest and spin up the sandbox. we'll aim to have network info from Priya and compliance docs from Marco by Friday.
[00:10:25] Jared: Sounds good. thanks everyone.
[00:10:28] Elena: Thanks — talk soon.

Notes on audio/transcription: occasional filler words, some proper nouns mis-transcribed in the auto transcript (e.g., "Redwood Dedicated" rendered as "Redwood Dedicate"). Links mentioned: onboarding runbook (https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/irw-activation), terraform starter repo (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-starter), SOC2 link will be shared via secure drive.

End of transcript.
